source.title: Non-toxigenic penicillin-resistant cutaneous C. diphtheriae infection: A case report and review of the literature
source.source_type: short report; single-patient case report with narrative literature review
source.journal: Journal of Infection and Public Health

governing_sources.ATOM_authority_1: literature.py — authoritative structural domain model, executed directly
governing_sources.ATOM_authority_2: literature_atoms.py — authoritative atom-kind sufficiency validator, executed directly
governing_sources.ATOM_authority_3: literature_atom.schema.json — authoritative serialization contract, validated with Draft 2020-12
governing_sources.ATOM_authority_5: example_atom.json — illustrative only, consulted without treating example values as evidence
governing_sources.large_source_support: large-source-ATOM-SEA.md — batching decision consulted; batching not required for this three-page source

protocol_version_note: The governing SEA file is named v4-compact but its internal H1 identifies Integrated Compact v3. Per project precedence, the named v4 project source was treated as governing; its operational requirements were followed as written.

consistency_review.finding: The susceptibility paragraph contains a visibly incomplete phrase ("the bacteria were penicillin and sensitive to erythromycin"). Penicillin resistance was not inferred from that fragment alone; it is independently stated in the title, summary, and authors’ highlighted discussion point.

schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom model has no dedicated case-report event/timeline atom kind, so non-quantitative clinical course events are represented as qualitative_result, method, intervention_description, exposure_description, or other as appropriate.

The model requires a quantitative_result object for atom_kind=adverse_event; the erythromycin nausea/vomiting event had no numeric effect estimate in the source, so it is represented as qualitative_result rather than fabricating a quantitative adverse-event estimate.
Secondary findings from cited studies are represented as other with the tag secondary_reported_result; they are not presented as primary-study quantitative_result atoms.
extraction_limitations: This is a single-patient case report with a brief narrative literature review; it does not support comparative efficacy estimates or incidence estimates.
No formal methods section, susceptibility testing method details, MIC values, antimicrobial doses, or complete microbiology workflow details are reported.
The literature-review summaries were extracted only as the authors’ secondary reports; the six cited primary sources were not independently read in this task.
All atoms remain needs_review because no human verification step is represented.
No external current-practice or regulatory verification was performed because @VERIFY was not activated.
